pr_title: Skip empty spans when updating text buffers
pr_body:
# Objective

Fixes #16521

## Solution

If an empty span is encountered (such as the default `Text` value), we skip it entirely when updating buffers. This prevents unnecessarily bailing when the font doesn't exist (ex: when the default font is disabled)

issue_context.title: Nested text spans are not rendered if the `default_font` feature is disabled
comments: This could be rephrased like "if **any** text span has an invalid font handle, the entire text does not render."
`TextPipeline::update_buffer` exits early if any font is not available. It will wait until all fonts are loaded.

I think the biggest issue to resolve for 0.15 is "spans with valid fonts nested under empty Text not rendering by default if there is no default font".

A fix that feels reasonable for that would be to skip empty spans / not fail out for "not yet loaded" fonts when text is empty. I'll give that a try.

The long term (likely harder) and more controversial fix would be to more effectively iteratively render text as fonts load. However this would result in unnecessary re-layouts + pop in. Idk if thats desirable.

review_comments: For correct indexing, this should go after `computed.entities.push(TextEntity { entity, depth });`.

Ah yeah. I thought I tested this properly, but it was setting the wrong span and I didn't know because the colors were the same. Sure enough, giving the spans different colors surfaced an indexing problem, and the reorder fixes it.
